children: The dollar could stretch its recent gains if Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh signals another rate hike is likely after Wednesday's decision, according to Societe Generale.

has been supported by a risk-averse market, though the move has been modest, the bank said. The DXY rose from 97.5 before the Gulf conflict began to 101.5 as it developed but has stayed below 100 since falling to 98 over the summer.

Higher energy costs and expectations that the conflict will drag on have not been enough to push the index back above 100, Societe Generale said. The firm pointed to improved optimism around growth expectations relative to the start of the conflict as one reason for the DXY's own resilience.

Markets will focus on how much guidance Warsh gives after the decision, said Kit Juckes of Societe Generale. If Warsh does not sound hawkish enough and investors begin doubting a second hike by year-end, the dollar could struggle to extend gains, Juckes said.
In that scenario, money could flow back into the Norwegian krone and Australian dollar as investors turn to the Bank of England and Bank of Japan meetings later this week, he said.
If Warsh instead signals a further hike is likely, the dollar has room to rise further, Juckes said. The yen's recent correction should also persist, unless the BoJ turns unusually hawkish.

Societe Generale's preferred trades for a “slightly hawkish” 25-basis-point hike are long USD/CHF and long AUD/NZD, Juckes said. The USD/CHF trade is a carry play, though Juckes noted the franc has a history of disappointing carry traders. The AUD/NZD trade rests partly on the view that copper prices have further room to rise.
Equity and bond selloffs have paused ahead of the Fed, BoE, and BoJ meetings, the note said, with FX positioning also being trimmed as investors take stock.

title: Dollar could extend gains on hawkish Warsh signal, SocGen says
